title: Vilasa 19. The Six Deities of Kheturi; Rupa Narayana; Virachandra's Travels
html:
Ramachandra Kaviraja brings Srinivasa back from samadhi (Radha's nose-ring); Shyamananda converts Sher Khan and the yogi Damodara; the passing of Gadadhara Dasa and Narahari, the memorial festivals at Katwa and Khanda; Jahnava's return from Vrindavana; the vanishing of the Kheturi deities, the finding of Gauranga's image in Vipradasa's granary and the abhisheka of the six deities on Phalguna Purnima; Mahaprabhu and his companions appear in the kirtana; Madhava Acharya, author of the Krishna-mangala, and Madhava Acharya, husband of Ganga; wonders on Jahnava's journey to Vrindavana; the service at Kheturi; the deliverance of Gurudasa Bhattacharya, Jagannatha Acharya and Chand Raya's former soldiers; the story of the pandita Rupa Narayana and the conversion of Raja Narasimha; Narottama reveals the sacred thread in his heart; Virachandra heals the blind Ramai, travels to Nilachala and Vrindavana and returns to Khardaha

1Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Nityananda!
Glory to Advaitachandra! Glory to the devotees of Gaura!

2Glory, glory to Srinivasa Acharya Thakura!
Glory, glory to Shyamananda, full of the rasa of prema!

3Glory, glory to Narottama Thakura Mahashaya!
Glory, glory to Ramachandra, the abode of virtues!

4Now I shall tell a little of the greatness of Ramachandra,
whose bhajana and grasp of truth have no equal.

5One day Srinivasa Acharya Mahashaya
was staying in Vana-Vishnupur, in the king's house.

6His two wives were with him;
understanding [his] signs, they did the work at once1.

7Having bathed and so on, he sat on his seat
and began the worship of his chosen deity.

8His own siddha name is Sri Mani Manjari;
in his mind he contemplated the blessed abode of Vrindavana.

9Absorbed in meditation, he entered samadhi,
and then the lila of Radha and Krishna became visible to him.

10He sees Radha and Krishna with all the sakhis
merrily sporting in the waters of the Yamuna.

11In the water play Sri Radhika became quite carried away:
the ring fell from her nose, and she did not notice2.

12When they had finished playing, [all] came up onto the bank,
and each began to put on her own clothes and ornaments.

13Then Sri Rupa Manjari looked at Radha
and did not see the ring in her nose.

14Sri Rupa Manjari signalled to Guna Manjari
and said, "Find the nose-ring and bring it quickly."

15Sri Guna Manjari, understanding the hint,
said to Mani Manjari with a smile:

16"Search in the waters of the Yamuna
and bring back Srimati's ornament."

17Having said this, all the sakhis went to the kunja,
while Sri Mani Manjari began to search.

18She searched for a long time and cannot find it;
she looks here and there, and her heart is troubled.

19Here meanwhile the two wives of Acharya Thakura,
seeing that his meditation did not break, grew anxious.

20The day went by, evening came, night fell;
however loudly they called out the Hari-nama —

21there is no breath in or out, the body does not stir;
seeing this, both were seized with fear3.

22The day went by, night came, and there is no consciousness;
seeing this, both weep aloud.

23The king heard of all this
and came in haste to see his master.

24Hearing of it, Vyasa Acharya, Sri Krishnavallabha
and the other devotees also came to see.

25Looking closely at Acharya Thakura's body,
they called to mind the states of Mahaprabhu4.

26The night passed, day came, the third prahara arrived5 —
and still Prabhu's body did not stir.

27Seeing this, the two wives of the Acharya
began to weep loudly.

28The king and all the devotees grew downcast;
"What has happened? What has happened?" they say, and their minds are not at rest.

29The devotees examined Prabhu's body at length
and understood that there was no cause to fear harm.

30All of them comforted the two wives of the guru;
then a thought arose in the Ishvari's mind6:

31"Ramachandra Kaviraja is Prabhu's power;
if he saw him, he would understand what state Prabhu is in."

32The Ishvari said, "O, listen, Maharaja:
bring Ramachandra quickly, do not delay."

33[The king] arranged to have Ramachandra brought;
meanwhile the night ended and morning came.

34And Ramachandra, [wishing] to see Prabhu,
came to the king's house at daybreak.

35His arrival was announced to the Ishvari,
and the king took the Kaviraja into the inner apartments.

36From a distance he bowed to the feet of his Prabhu
and touched his head to the feet of both of Prabhu's wives.

37Looking at Prabhu, Ramachandra said, "There is nothing to worry about:
after a while the Gosani will regain outer consciousness."

38Having said this, Ramachandra sat down in meditation
and in his siddha body contemplated his chosen deity.

39His own siddha name is Sri Karuna Manjari;
in that body he went to the abode of Radha and Krishna.

40Bowing to Radha and Krishna and to all the sakhis,
he went to the bank of the Yamuna.

41He sees Sri Mani Manjari standing in the water;
without delay he too went down into the Yamuna.

42He sees the nose-ring lying covered by a lotus leaf;
he picked it up and quickly gave it into Mani Manjari's hand.

43Getting the nose-ring, Sri Mani Manjari was delighted
and said, "Friend, let us go to the kunja, quickly!"

44From there they went to the kunja
and handed the nose-ring to Guna Manjari.

45Guna Manjari gave it into Rupa Manjari's hand,
and Rupa Manjari put it on Radha's nose.

46A lovely form, and on it clothes and ornaments —
whoever sees the Divine Couple has his mind stolen.

47Having beheld the sweet form of the Divine Couple,
Ramachandra regained outer consciousness and then rose.

48Calling out the name of Hari, he began to recite praises;
and, regaining outer consciousness, Srinivasa rose and sat up.

49"What a form I have seen!" he says, and weeps;
embracing Ramachandra, he opened his eyes.

50Ramachandra fell at the feet of his Prabhu,
and all the devotees together cried, "Hari! Hari!"

51Then Sri Ishvari and Sri Gauranga-priya
went with glad hearts and cooked.

52Many kinds of rice and dishes were cooked;
having offered them [to the deity], the Acharya ate.

53From Prabhu's plate Ramachandra took prasada;
afterwards all the devotees ate prasada.

54Having rinsed their mouths, all came to rest
and spent the night in talk of Krishna.

55The greatness of Ramachandra Kaviraja is boundless;
the little I have described is according to Prabhu's words.

56Now I shall write a little of the greatness of Shyamananda,
to whom even the gods cannot find a limit.

57From Vraja, Shyamananda, by way of Gauda,
passing through Garerhat, came to Ambika.

58With great joy he beheld Mahaprabhu
and prostrated himself before Hridaya Chaitanya7.

59He related everything that had happened in Vrindavana;
hearing it, he was greatly gladdened.

60Hearing of the theft of the books, he was grieved8;
for some time Shyamananda stayed there.

61After a while he received a letter
and, seeing the news that the books had been found, rejoiced.

62Then, taking leave of his Sri Guru,
he went to his own country, Utkala.

63Coming to his native village of Dharenda9,
he revealed prema-bhakti in all its fullness.

64He spread the nama-sankirtana
and delivered many robbers and pashandis.

65One day Shyamananda with the sankirtana
was going about to various places with a joyful heart.

66There was a deputy of the king, a Pathan named Sher Khan;
hearing the sankirtana, he burned with ceaseless anger.

67He forbids the performance of sankirtana —
Shyamananda does not listen and carries on the sankirtana.

68In anger that robber yavana, taking [other] yavanas with him,
smashed the khols and karatalas and threw them away.

69Then Shyamananda in anger gave a terrible roar,
and fear entered the hearts of all the yavanas.

70The beards and moustaches of the yavanas were all burnt off;
they vomited blood, and all were prostrated.

71Shyamananda then went to his own place,
and all [of them] too went off to their own places.

72The next day Shyamananda, with great pomp,
gathered many bands of sankirtana.

73Performing kirtana through various places,
all went along full of joy.

74Seeing this, the robber yavana Sher Khan came in haste
and bowed many times at Shyamananda's feet:

75"O Shyamananda Prabhu, have mercy on me!
I have committed an offence — give me shelter at your feet."

76What befell him for breaking up the sankirtana
he began to relate in brief:

77"My beard was burnt, blood came from my nose and mouth;
[but] when I tell of the dream, my heart weeps.

78First I saw a terrible form;
it struck me on the cheek and said, 'Hey, you wretched yavana!

79I am your Allah, Ahad incarnate10' —
and with these words it showed a golden form:

80'My name is Sri Chaitanya, the refuge of all;
Shyamananda is my great devotee.

81From him you will take the mantra of Krishna,
or else you are bound for hell.'

82I saw a wondrous form — my eyes cannot contain it;
the tears of my eyes cannot be stopped.

83You, Prabhu, are the teacher of the world; have mercy on me:
there is none so low as I — give me the shade of your feet."

84Thus he pleaded humbly in many ways;
seeing his humility, Shyamananda showed him favour.

85All this I heard from the lips of my Prabhu
and, taking her command upon my head, have described it11.

86Having delivered the yavana, Shyamananda went to Rayani
and, going there, spread prema-bhakti.

87That village lies on the bank of the river Suvarnarekha;
there lives a raja named Achyutananda.

88He has two sons, named Rasika and Murari12;
Shyamananda showed them great mercy.

89In Balarampur, in Sri Nrisimhapur
and in Gopivallabhapur he made many disciples.

90In Gopivallabhapur he gave out prema abundantly
and entrusted the service of Sri Govinda to Rasika13.

91The greatness of Rasikananda is boundless;
he delivered many robber yavanas.

92His many disciples cannot be counted;
[let] whoever is fortunate describe them.

93One day Shyamananda in Gopivallabhapur
was sitting together with the devotees.

94At that time an eminent sannyasi came,
and he had a long debate with Shyamananda.

95This yogi, a Vedantist, knew many shastras;
the debate with Shyamananda went on for many days.

96[Shyamananda] refuted the yogi's advaita-vada in debate
and by the teaching of the Gosvamis established dvaita.

97In the debate the yogi was defeated
and inwardly praised Shyamananda highly.

98At night the yogi had a dream:
Shyamananda is a jewel among great personalities.

99He had been a cowherd, a gopa, and became a brahmana14 —
such is the power of bhajana, as everyone knows.

100The next day the yogi, rising in the morning,
came and fell at Shyamananda's feet:

101"There is no sinner in the world as low as I;
have mercy and deliver me, a sinner."

102Then Shyamananda, a jewel among great personalities,
placed his feet on the yogi's head.

103In his mercy he gave him initiation into the mantra of Krishna
and explained all the rules of sadhana.

104That yogi's name is Damodara;
he became devoted to the bhajana of Sri Krishna.

105One day, when Shyamananda was in seclusion,
Damodara came and prostrated himself before him.

106He sees Shyamananda's form shining brilliantly,
and a radiant sacred thread glittering on his body.

107At that moment Rasika and the other devotees came;
prostrating themselves, they offered many praises.

108Shyamananda, hiding the sacred thread
and concealing his radiance, began the nama-sankirtana.

109This Mahashaya is filled with the avesha of Advaita Prabhu15;
in many ways he distributes prema-bhakti to people.

110Thus he delivered a multitude of pashandis
and gave [them] prema-bhakti.

111Shyamananda's bhajana has no equal;
his siddha name is Kanaka Manjari.

112What do I know of Shyamananda's many deeds?
And the little I have written, I wrote in obedience to the guru's command.

113Listen, listen, listeners, be attentive:
give heed to what I shall now relate.

114The great festivals that took place at Katwa and at Khanda
I did not describe before — now I shall describe them all16.

115The Thakurani commanded me to describe them;
the guru's command is the strongest — I took it to heart.

116When they heard that Vishnupriya Thakurani had disappeared [from the world],
the grief of the devotees was beyond words17.

117Then Gadadhara Dasa and Narahari Sarakara —
how much both of them grieved I cannot say.

118Little by little Gadadhara Dasa grew very weak
and within a short time vanished from the world.

119He disappeared on the krishna-ashtami of the month of Karttika;
Yadunandana and the other devotees grieved greatly.

120Hearing that Prabhu Gadadhara Dasa had disappeared,
Narahari Sarakara lamented long.

121Raghunandana, Sulochana — all the devotees there were —
with the tears of them all the earth was soaked.

122Thus Narahari, stricken with grief,
one day vanished from everyone's sight —

123on the krishna-ekadashi of the month of Agrahayana;
seeing his departure, all weep.

124How Raghunandana and Sulochana grieved
I cannot describe even in small part.

125By Prabhu's will Raghunandana recovered
and resolved to go to Katwa.

126Taking Lochana with him, Sri Raghunandana
came to the town of Katwa18.

127Sri Yadunandana Chakravarti Mahashaya
is a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa, very dear to him.

128To him Sri Raghunandana went;
seeing Sri Gauranga, he rejoiced greatly19.

129Many times he prostrated himself in obeisance,
[and then] went to Yadunandana.

130Embracing, both bowed down full length
and, speaking of the departure [of their masters], wept long.

131By Prabhu's will both grew calm
and, sitting together, fixed the day of the festival.

132Then, having arranged everything for the festival here,
Raghunandana went to Khanda, remembering Prabhu's feet.

133There too preparations for the festival began,
and letters of invitation were sent everywhere.

134Gadadhara Dasa and Thakura Narahari —
for both there will be a great memorial festival20.

135All the mahantas received two invitations
and went to the town of Katwa in great joy.

136Some days beforehand Raghunandana gladly
came to Katwa together with Lochana and others.

137Raghunandana and the others set to work
and put everything in particular order.

138Now I shall tell of the arrival of the mahantas;
I give only an indication — it cannot all be described.

139As many branches of Sri Mahaprabhu as came,
I shall only name them, each one separately.

140Sripati, Srinidhi, Vaninatha, Vasu, Kavichandra,
Ramadasa, Sanjaya and Vidyananda came21;

141Kamalakanta, Vishnudasa, Sri Chandrashekhara;
Chaitanya Dasa and Sridhara the kirtaniya came22;

142Nayana Pandita and Kavi Karnapura,
Janakinatha, Gopala Dasa, Acharya Purandara.

143All the branches of Sri Nityananda Prabhu came too;
I shall name a few according to my understanding.

144Murari, Chaitanya Dasa, Raghunatha Vaidya,
Upadhyaya Narayana — and I, the unfortunate23;

145Sanatana, Krishnadasa and Manohara,
Nakadi, Gopala Dasa and Mahidhara;

146Ramachandra Kaviraja24, Vasanta, Lavani,
Hariharananda, Kanu Thakura, a jewel of virtues;

147Ramasena, Jnanadasa and Damodara;
Sri Kumuda and Pitambara came;

148Nrisimha Chaitanya and Vrindavana Dasa,
who brought forth the Sri Chaitanya-mangala25;

149Prabhu Virachandra; Madhava Acharya, a jewel of virtues,
whose wife is Ganga, the daughter of Nityananda;

150two Mahashayas came, Jagannatha and Madhava,
who are called Jagai and Madhai.

151Thus I have named the companions of Nityananda Prabhu;
now I shall tell of the arrival of the companions of Advaita.

152Vanamali Dasa, Vijaya, Lokanatha Pandita,
Bholanatha, Hridayananda Sena, Murari Pandita;

153Kanu Pandita, Sri Haridasa Brahmachari,
Krishnadasa, Janardana Dasa, worthy of bhakti;

154Ananta Dasa, Narayana, the excellent Yadava Dasa,
Haricharana, Raghunatha, Sri Rama Acharya.

155Sri Madhava Acharya came, full of the rasa of bhakti,
whose singing of the Krishna-mangala is supremely sweet26;

156Achyutananda, Krishna Mishra, Prabhu Sri Gopala —
the sons of Advaita Prabhu, full of compassion.

157All the branches of Gadadhara Pandita Gosani came;
I shall name a few according to my understanding27:

158Chaitanya-vallabha Dasa, Bhagavata Acharya,
Pushpa Gopala, Gopala Dasa, Sri Hari Acharya,

159Sri Harsha, Raghu Mishra and Lakshminatha,
Jagannatha of Kashthakata and Raghunatha28.

160The Pandita Gosani's brother is Vaninatha;
his son is Nayanananda Mishra Mahashaya,

161the Pandita Gosani's disciple and his power;
he too came to Katwa with gladness in his heart.

162As many devotees came — who can count them?
I have given only a general indication.

163All the mahantas and adhikaris there were in various places —
all came, filled with great delight.

164All beheld the place where Prabhu took sannyasa29,
and tears flowed ceaselessly from their eyes.

165From there they went to the courtyard of the temple
and, seeing the image of Sri Gauranga, rejoiced at heart.

166With glad hearts they prostrate themselves
and, full of delight, began the sankirtana.

167All the mahantas dance in boundless bliss;
tears of prema stream unceasingly from their eyes.

168Then, having seen the food offering and the arati,
all took prasada with joyful hearts.

169After staying some days at Katwa,
they set out for Khanda in boundless bliss.

170Raghunandana, having come to Khanda some days earlier,
had gladly put the arrangements in order.

171All the mahantas came to Khanda,
and each was given lodging in a fitting place.

172All the mahantas, staying some days at Khanda,
held a great festival and were very happy.

173One day in the sankirtana all the mahantas
dance and sing in perfect bliss.

174At that time a blind man came there
and by the mercy of Prabhu Virachandra received his sight.

175Crying, "Blessed! Blessed!" all rejoiced;
I shall relate it in detail further on.

176For some days the mahantas stayed there,
and then, taking leave, went to their homes.

177Having seen off the mahantas, Sri Raghunandana —
how much sorrow he felt cannot be told.

178What shall I write? What comes first and what after, I cannot judge;
I only write, taking the Thakurani's command upon my head30.

179Listen, listen, listeners, with one mind:
now I shall describe the deeds of Narottama.

180The festival held at the manifestation of Sri Gauranga and Sri Vallavikanta
I have described in detail31.

181Afterwards I only named the six deities;
[now] the guru has commanded me to describe the second abhisheka.

182What was the order of the abhisheka of the six deities
I shall now describe — all will be pleased.

183O listeners, all give heed:
[I shall tell] all the reasons for the second abhisheka.

184All this I shall describe by the Ishvari's command,
contemplating her feet in the sky of my heart.

185All that I saw with my own eyes I shall describe —
that which pleased all the mahantas.

186For the second time the Ishvari with her companions
came back from Vrindavana again to Kheturi32.

187And I was with the Ishvari at every moment:
never did I leave these feet.

188The Mahashaya, hearing of the Thakurani's arrival,
came with the Kaviraja to meet her.

189Seeing the Thakurani, Narottama and Ramachandra
fell to the ground, prostrating themselves.

190Having bowed, they asked after her welfare
and carried her in a palanquin to their home.

191The Thakurani, before Sri Gauranga and Sri Vallavikanta-raya,
prostrates herself with a joyful heart.

192Looking at the sacred images, she was overcome with prema;
tears ran down her face.

193After a while the Devi grew calm
and, having bathed and performed her daily rites, took prasada.

194Sri Ishvari rested a while,
washed her face and sat on her seat.

195Ramachandra and Narottama came;
having bowed, both sat on their seats.

196Talk of Vrindavana began;
she gave Narottama Lokanatha's blessing.

197Hearing his own Prabhu's blessing, the Mahashaya,
remembering his feet, wept bitterly.

198She gave Ramachandra the blessing of Gopala Bhatta;
he, remembering his feet, began to weep.

199Having conveyed the blessings of Jiva Gosani and others,
Sri Ishvari showed favour to them both.

200Having stayed happily at Kheturi two to four days,
the Ishvari went from there to Yajigrama.

201Hearing of the Ishvari's arrival, Srinivasa
came out in great joy to meet her.

202Bowing at Sri Ishvari's feet,
he gladly brought her to his house.

203When bathing, eating and the rest were done,
the talk of Vrindavana began.

204She gave Srinivasa the blessing of Bhatta Gosani;
remembering Prabhu's feet, he began to weep.

205Learning all about Jiva Gosvami and the others,
he rejoiced at heart, and tears of joy flowed from his eyes.

206Having stayed some two days at Yajigrama, the Ishvari
soon came to Khardaha.

207Hearing that the Ishvari had returned from Vrindavana,
the people of Khardaha rejoiced.

208So the Thakurani went to Khardaha;
and here a certain feeling arose in Narottama.

209One day the Mahashaya, having finished the evening arati,
was gazing at the two sacred images.

210Looking at the images without the Beloved33,
he felt a divine feeling awaken in his heart:

211"Will such a blessed day ever come for me,
when I shall see with these eyes the images of the Divine Couple?

212How great will be the joy if I see the Divine Couple —
I shall not be able to put it into words.

213Today there has arisen in my heart [the wish]
to install further images of Krishna together with the Beloved.

214Seeing the household of Sri Krishna34,
let the body be refreshed, let eyes and mind be purified.

215When will my Prabhu bring about such a day for me,
that, seeing Krishna's household, I may be immersed in bliss?"

216Thinking thus, the Mahashaya became distraught;
bereft of outer consciousness, he passed the greater part of the night.

217By Prabhu's will sleep overcame him,
and in a dream Bhagavan appeared to him.

218Gauranga and Vallavikanta, smiling, said,
"O Narottama, your desire is fulfilled.

219You have resolved to install further images —
seeing Krishna's household, you will float in bliss35.

220To fulfil the desires of devotees is my task;
you are a supreme devotee, your desire will be fulfilled.

221Behold, O Narottama:
I have assumed six forms, together with the Beloved.

222These six forms you are to install;
I shall tell you their names — listen.

223Gauranga, Vallavikanta, and also Sri Krishna,
Vraja-mohana, Radha-ramana, Radha-kanta — these are the six.

224O Narottama, in the forms of Gauranga and Vallavikanta
I have dwelt in your house with great joy.

225[Now] these two forms of mine have vanished,
and the temple now stands empty.

226Quickly bring forth the six deities again —
seeing them, all people will rejoice.

227At the time of the abhisheka of the six deities
these two forms of mine will be united [with them]:

228Gaura-raya will merge into Gauranga,
Vallavikanta will become one with Vallavikanta36.

229In these six forms I shall reside;
whoever sees them — all living beings will be saved."

230Having said this, Bhagavan vanished,
and at that very moment Narottama woke and sat up.

231At the sight of Bhagavan he was beside himself with bliss,
and the grief of losing sight of him had no limit.

232Then came the time of the mangala-arati,
and the Mahashaya came to the temple doors.

233Ramachandra Kaviraja met him there;
the pujari opened the doors with a glad heart.

234They see there are no sacred images in the temple!
"What has happened? What has happened?" they cry, deeply pained.

235Seeing the empty shrine, the Mahashaya began to weep,
and Ramachandra Kaviraja was grief-stricken.

236Then the sound of weeping arose:
all weep in distress, and the earth was soaked [with tears].

237By Prabhu's will the Mahashaya grew calm
and little by little calmed everyone37.

238He told Ramachandra his dream:
"Make arrangements for the abhisheka of the six deities.

239Have Acharya Thakura brought from Vishnupura
and gladly do all that is fitting."

240Having said this, he then told the pujari,
"Worship the two deities in the shalagrama38.

241Until the deities appear again,
until then worship [them] in the shalagrama."

242Having said this, he was sitting with Ramachandra —
and at that moment a letter from the Acharya came.

243Receiving the letter, Narottama was glad;
in the letter is written: "The Acharya is going to Vrindavana."

244Learning that the Acharya had gone to Vrindavana,
he was ever anxious, and his heart had no rest.

245One day Narottama said to Ramachandra,
"Go to Vrindavana and bring back the Acharya."

246Then Ramachandra Kavi[raja] went to Vrindavana,
and Narottama set out for Nilachala.

247He beheld Jagannatha and the places of Mahaprabhu's lila,
and then went on to Shyamananda.

248Having stayed [there] some time, he went to Gauda
and travelled through Khardaha, Shantipur, Ambika.

249By way of Navadvipa, Khanda, the town of Katwa
and Ekachakra he came home39.

250Coming home, he resolved to install the deities,
and at night Narottama saw a dream:

251Gauranga, Vallavikanta, and also Sri Krishna,
Vraja-mohana, Radha-kanta, Radha-ramana — these six.

252How his heart rejoiced on seeing
the six deities together with the Beloved cannot be described.

253Having seen the dream, Narottama woke and sat up
and, shedding tears of joy, passed [the rest of] the night.

254At daybreak, having done his morning duties,
he made great preparations for fashioning the deities.

255Stone was brought, craftsmen were summoned,
and he had six deities carved together with the Beloved40.

256The five images of Krishna turned out excellent,
but the image of Gaura would not take shape properly.

257However hard they try, the image will not form;
seeing this, Thakura Mahashaya grew very anxious.

258"Gauranga! Gauranga!" he cries aloud;
and in a dream Sri Chaitanya appeared to him.

259At night the Mahashaya saw a dream:
Sri Chaitanya, sitting at his head, says softly:

260"Listen attentively, child Narottama:
however hard you try, my image will not take shape.

261In this image I shall not reside;
I shall tell you of an image that I made myself.

262Before my sannyasa I fashioned an image of myself
and, without anyone knowing, sank it in the Ganga.

263You are the embodiment of my prema; to you I show favour:
I have placed that deity in Vipradasa's granary41."

264Having said this, Sri Chaitanya vanished;
waking, Narottama sees that day has dawned.

265Rising and doing his morning duties, the Mahashaya
asks people where Vipradasa's house is.

266A man came up to Narottama and said,
"Vipradasa is a rich man who lives in these parts.

267He has much grain — paddy, mustard and the rest;
he is always trading in grain."

268Hearing this, Narottama went to his house;
seeing the Mahashaya, Vipradasa bows down.

269He says, "Why have you come here?"
The Mahashaya says, "There is a particular need."

270Narottama says, "I shall go into your granary."
Vipradasa says, "That must not be done:

271there is the danger of many kinds of snakes;
when they see a man, they hiss loudly.

272For fear of the snakes no one can go in there;
there is much paddy [lying] there from long ago."

273Narottama says, "Do not worry at all:
when I go in, all the snakes will flee."

274Having said this, Narottama went into the granary,
and the snakes then vanished.

275From the granary he lifted out the image of Chaitanya;
seeing it, all the people were rid of every distress.

276From then on the fear of snakes ceased,
and joy blossomed in Vipradasa's heart.

277Then Vipradasa with his whole family came
and took refuge at the feet of Thakura Mahashaya.

278Narottama installed the image of Gauranga42;
seeing its form, all were filled with joy.

279The image of Gauranga that [people] had seen with their eyes before —
"This is the very same," they say, "it is no different at all."

280The Mahashaya, receiving no letter from Srinivasa Acharya,
was ever anxious, and his heart was restless.

281At that time a letter was put into the Mahashaya's hand:
"The Acharya has come to Vishnupura with Ramachandra."

282Now Ramachandra, together with Acharya Prabhu,
went by way of Khardaha and Shantipur to Ambika.

283By way of Navadvipa and Khanda they came to Yajigrama,
and from there set out for Katwa.

284There they beheld Mahaprabhu
and, staying a few days, went to Teliya Budhari.

285Hearing that they had come to Budhari, the Mahashaya
went with a few companions to Ramachandra's house.

286Hearing from afar of Narottama's arrival,
the Acharya came out with Ramachandra to meet him.

287When Narottama bowed to Srinivasa Acharya,
he embraced him and could not let him go.

288Ramachandra bowed to Narottama;
he, bowing in return, embraced him.

289Govinda came and bowed to Narottama;
he, embracing him, held him to his heart.

290Then all went into the house
and, sitting down, talked of Vrindavana.

291[They told] how the Gosvamis had shown favour to Ramachandra,
and conveyed Lokanatha's blessing to Narottama.

292Narottama, crying "Prabhu!", wept
and with great difficulty steadied his mind.

293He told all about the fashioning of the deities
and related the whole story of how Gauranga was found.

294Hearing this, the Acharya and all the others were glad at heart
and all cried out together, "Blessed! Blessed!"

295Srinivasa said, "Take Ramachandra and the others,
go to Kheturi and begin the preparations for the abhisheka.

296I shall come soon; you set out."
Hearing this, he took everyone and came to Kheturi.

297Coming to Kheturi, he made all the preparations
and appointed a separate person to each task.

298Wherever the companions of Sri Mahaprabhu were,
he sent letters of invitation everywhere.

299On the lunar day of Phalguna Purnima
[it was resolved] to perform the abhisheka and seat the deities on the throne.

300Day and night the sankirtana went on;
hearing it, the pashandis felt as if struck by a thunderbolt.

301Now I shall tell of the arrival of the mahantas;
listen, all of you, attentively.

302Srinivasa, Ramachandra and Sri Govinda,
Vyasa Acharya, Krishnavallabha, Divyasimha, Premananda;

303Karnapura, Vamshidasa and Shyamadasa;
from Budhuipara came Sri Gopala Dasa;

304Sri Gokula Vidyavanta of Kanchana-Nagariya43;
of all the people who came there was no end.

305With Rasika, Murari and other devotees
Shyamananda came from Utkala to Kheturi.

306From Khardaha came Jahnava Ishvari;
I shall name some of the devotees who came with her:

307her son, Prabhu Virachandra, rare to find in the world44;
her son-in-law Madhava Acharya, the husband of Ganga;

308Krishnadasa, Suryadasa and Raghupati,
Murari, Chaitanya Dasa, Sri Jiva Pandita;

309Nrisimha, Gauranga Dasa, Kamalakara Piplai,
Minaketana Ramadasa, Shankara, Kanai;

310Narayana, Sanatana, Nakadi, Manohara,
Gopala, Vrindavana, Ramasena, Damodara;

311Jnanadasa, Kumuda and Pitambara;
Ramachandra, Nrisimha and Haladhara came.

312As many devotees came — how many shall I name?
I shall name a few according to my understanding45.

313In the village of Halisahar lived Nayana Bhaskara;
he came to Kheturi together with Raghunatha Acharya.

314Hridaya Chaitanya with his own devotees
came to Kheturi in great joy.

315From Shantipur came two Mahashayas,
Gopala and Achyutananda, the sons of Advaita.

316As many devotees came with them —
now I shall name some of them:

317Kanu Pandita, Vishnudasa, Acharya Janardana,
Kamadeva, Vanamali Dasa, Narayana,

318Purushottama, Shyamadasa, Madhava Acharya,
whose singing of the Krishna-mangala robs all of their composure —

319the dearest disciples of Sri Chaitanya and Advaita:
by Chaitanya's mercy the bonds of worldly life fell [from them].

320From Navadvipa Sripati, Srinidhi and others
came to Kheturi full of delight.

321Yadunandana of Katwa, bringing devotees with him,
came to Kheturi together with Krishnadasa of Akaihat.

322From Khanda came Sri Raghunandana,
bringing with him Lochana Dasa and other devotees46.

323Shivananda, Vaninatha, Sri Hari Acharya,
Jita Mishra, Kashinatha, Bhagavata Acharya,

324the Pandita Gosani's nephew Sri Nayanananda,
Pushpa Gopala, Gopala Dasa and Dhruvananda,

325Raghu Mishra, Sri Uddhava, Jagannatha of Kashthakata —
as many came, how many shall I name?

326Wherever the devotees of Sri Krishna Chaitanya were,
little by little all came and gathered at Kheturi.

327Narottama showed great honour to all
and gave each lodging in a fitting place.

328Sri Govinda, Sri Santosha and some others
were appointed to the service of all [the guests].

329Having finished their meal and the rest, all the mahantas
went to sleep at night in perfect joy.

330In the night Narottama sees a dream:
Sri Chaitanya comes and speaks these words to him:

331"Tomorrow in the great sankirtana with the devotees
I shall dance — all will see it with their own eyes."

332Having said this, he placed his feet on Narottama's head,
and Gauranga, Sri Hari, vanished.

333In great bliss Narottama woke quickly
and saw that the night had almost turned to dawn.

334Thakura Mahashaya and the others, having done their morning duties,
hastily began the great abhisheka.

335Srinivasa Acharya went to Jahnava
and, bowing, received her permission.

336Narottama made many obeisances
and one by one received the permission of all the mahantas.

337Having received the permission of all the mahantas,
he gladly began the work.

338Narottama Thakura, immersed in prema,
with a joyful heart sheds tears unceasingly.

339The names of the deities that he had received in the dream —
all those names he then began to pronounce:

340"Gauranga, Vallavikanta, and also Sri Krishna,
Vraja-mohana, Radha-ramana, Radha-kanta — these six."

341Thus in the verse composed by Sri Thakura Mahashaya:
*"Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Sri Krishna, Vraja-mohana,
Radha-ramana, O Radha, Radha-kanta — obeisance to You!"*

342According to the rules of the great abhisheka of Sri Krishna
he performed the abhisheka of the six deities with a joyful heart.

343On the lunar day of Phalguna Purnima, having performed the abhisheka,
he seated the sacred deities on the throne.

344Taking various clothes and ornaments,
Srinivasa with gladness of heart dresses the deities.

345Then, looking at the sacred deities, all the mahantas —
streams flow from their eyes, and their joy has no end.

346The gods from heaven shower flowers;
cries of "Glory! Glory! Glory!" resound unceasingly.

347The sounds of various instruments captivate everyone's mind;
the brahmanas recite the Vedas in sweet voices.

348Phalguna Purnima is the great festival of the Dola-yatra
and the birthday of Mahaprabhu: the celebration has no bounds47.

349According to the rules of the ten-syllable mantra of Sri Gopala
he worshipped the six deities with a joyful mind48.

350Having completed the puja, he performed the arati;
seeing it, all the people rejoiced.

351When the arati was over, all the mahantas
in supreme joy prostrate themselves on the ground.

352Narottama, swimming in an ocean of happiness,
rolling on the ground, bows down with this mantra.

353Thus in his own verse:
*"Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Sri Krishna, Vraja-mohana,
Radha-ramana, O Radha, Radha-kanta — obeisance to You!"*

354Srinivasa in great joy bowed down
and has many kinds of foods brought.

355Arranging the offerings separately [for each deity],
Srinivasa with a glad heart offers them.

356After some time he gave [water] for rinsing the mouth,
offered tambula and opened the doors.

357Jahnava Ishvari, coming and seeing the deities,
bows again and again with fervour in her joy49.

358Then Srinivasa Acharya, coming out into the courtyard,
falling to the ground, bows again and again.

359He bows again and again to the companions of Mahaprabhu;
all embrace him, with tears of joy [streaming] from their eyes.

360Srinivasa bows at the feet of Sri Jahnava,
and she showed him great favour.

361Sri Jahnava asked Srinivasa,
"How did you perform the worship of Sri Gauranga?"

362He said, "By the command of the Gosvamis
I worshipped Chaitanya with the mantra of the Divine Couple, Radha and Krishna.

363The Gosvamis commanded that Chaitanya be worshipped
according to the rules of worship with the ten-syllable Gopala mantra."

364"Good!" said Jahnava, and praises [this] before all:
"Chaitanya Gosani is Radha and Krishna, the Divine Couple in one form"50.

365Having said this, Sri Jahnava fell silent;
Narottama came and bowed at her feet.

366Sri Ishvari showed favour to Narottama;
Narottama bowed to the companions of Chaitanya.

367The companions of Chaitanya with joyful hearts
embraced Narottama and cannot let him go.

368Sri Ishvari commanded Srinivasa,
"Give the sacred garlands and sandal paste to all the devotees there are."

369Srinivasa, bringing garlands and sandal paste as prasada,
gave them to Prabhu's companions, to each separately.

370Then he gave them to all the devotees,
and all were adorned with the sacred garlands and sandal paste.

371All the mahantas gave Sri Narottama
permission to begin the sankirtana.

372Then Narottama, bowing to all,
began the sankirtana with delight.

373First Devidasa plays on the khol;
in rhythm Gauranga Dasa plays the karatalas.

374Vallabha, Gokula and all the other devotees
began the sankirtana in sweet voices.

375All the devotees of Chaitanya, coming to the kirtana,
dance with arms raised, crying, "Gauranga!"

376Sri Gaurangachandra is immersed in the mood of Sri Radha —
of that mood he sings songs, filled with bliss.

377Narottama's voice, supremely sweet,
drew Gorachanda — he could not hold back.

378By the power of the bhakti of the great devotee Narottama
Gaura-raya appeared together with his companions:

379Nityananda, Advaita, Srivasa, Gadadhara,
Sri Murari, Haridasa, Svarupa Damodara;

380taking with him Rupa, Sanatana, Gauridasa and others,
he dances in the sankirtana, filled with joy.

381At that moment all forgot themselves;
streams flow from their eyes, all dance in joy.

382Taking with him Sri Achyutananda and all the devotees,
the Son of Shachi dances.

383Of all the devotees there, none has outer consciousness;
in bliss Advaita, Gauranga and Nitai dance.

384Who can understand Prabhu's transcendent lila?
As he appeared, so he vanished.

385No longer seeing Prabhu with his companions in the sankirtana,
all, regaining outer consciousness, weep bitterly.

386Narottama, Shyamananda and Srinivasa
roll on the ground, weep and heave deep sighs.

387Again and again, swooning, they fall to the ground;
their faces are bathed in the tears of their eyes.

388Srinivasa Acharya and all the others grew calm,
but the Mahashaya, crying "Gora!", weeps and finds no rest.

389Sri Achyutananda and all the devotees of Gaura,
consoling Narottama, calmed his heart:

390"Gaura-raya, with the companions of Nityananda and Advaita,
subject to your prema, let us all see him."

391All, embracing, bow at one another's feet;
what joy there was cannot be described.

392Srinivasa and Narottama, bowing at Achyuta's feet,
say, "Sprinkle coloured powder on Prabhu's body"51.

393Having said this, they had much powder brought here,
and Sri Jahnava sprinkled the powder on the body of the sacred image.

394Achyuta, Gopala, Narottama, Srinivasa,
Virachandra, Shyamananda, Ramachandra Dasa,

395Hridaya Chaitanya and Sri Raghunandana —
and how many [other] devotees there were, who can count? —

396all come and sprinkle powder on the body of the sacred image;
what joy there was cannot be written.

397Having sprinkled powder on the deity, all the mahantas
sprinkle powder on one another — their happiness has no end.

398They sing of Krishna's lila and ceaselessly throw powder —
in all ten directions water and land turned crimson.

399Having finished the kirtana, all the mahantas
eat prasada with great delight.

400Many foods — those that are chewed, sucked, licked and drunk52 —
all ate with joyful hearts.

401Evening came; all saw the arati
and for some time performed nama-sankirtana.

402To perform the abhisheka on Mahaprabhu's birthday,
they brought Gaura-raya into the courtyard.

403At Sri Ishvari's command Acharya Srinivasa
began the abhisheka with delight in his heart.

404According to the rules of [the festival of] Sri Krishna's birth
he worships Gaurangachand with gladness in his heart.

405Meditating on the Divine Couple, Sri Radha and Krishna, as described in the Padma[-purana], he worshipped [him] with the sixteen offerings, glad at heart53.

406Krishna and Gaura are one; whoever thinks of a difference here
goes to hell, and for him there is no deliverance.

407Having offered food, they laid the deity to rest,
and all the mahantas ate prasada54.

408Resting with gladness of heart,
all spent the night rapt in songs of Krishna's lila.

409Having seen the mangala-arati,
all went off to their own affairs.

410Staying here that day and taking prasada,
on the next day all took leave and departed.

411What grief Narottama felt at that time
I am unable to write even in part.

412Narottama's order of service is wonderful indeed;
who is able to describe how everything was arranged?

413Sri Lochana Dasa is born of a vaidya family;
he is a disciple of Sri Narahari and lives in Srikhanda55.

414The songs of the Chaitanya-mangala composed by him
are always sung in Narottama's house.

415First the Sri Chaitanya-mangala is sung,
and after that the Krishna-mangala is sung.

416The singing of the Sri Krishna-mangala is wonderful indeed:
whoever hears it, his heart melts and tears of joy flow.

417The Tenth Canto of the Srimad Bhagavata
Madhava Acharya rendered [in verse] in many metres.

418I shall describe a little of the virtues of Madhava Acharya,
whose character and virtues are known throughout the world.

419Durgadasa Mishra, a mine of all virtues,
a Vedic brahmana, lived in the town of Nadia.

420His wife's name was Sri Vijaya;
she bore two sons, abodes of virtue.

421The elder was Sanatana, the younger Parashara Kalidasa56;
supreme panditas, abodes of all virtues.

422Sanatana's wife was named Mahamaya;
she bore an only daughter, Vishnupriya.

423An only daughter, and no other children;
she was given in marriage to Sri Krishna Chaitanyachandra.

424Kalidasa Mishra's wife was named Vidhumukhi;
she bore a jewel of a son, an abode of all virtues.

425Leaving his only son, Kalidasa
left the earth and took up his abode in heaven.

426Vidhumukhi, with her son named Madhava in her arms,
became a widow at a young age.

427In the eighth year from conception Madhava was invested with the sacred thread57,
and he began to study various shastras.

428Having studied various shastras, he became a pandita
and became known by the title "Acharya".

429At the time of the abhisheka of Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu
Madhava Acharya went to Srivasa's house58.

430Seeing the form of Gauranga, he went mad [with love],
and from then on he became a devotee of Chaitanya.

431On the day when Sri Chaitanya
loudly instructed the devotees in his own Hari-nama —

432on that day Madhava was in that place,
and the sound of the maha-mantra entered his ears.

433Hearing the Name, he felt prema awaken
and prostrated himself at Chaitanya's feet.

434Sri Chaitanya Prabhu, showing him favour,
lifted his foot and placed it on his head.

435Madhava asked Prabhu about the rules of [chanting] the Name;
Prabhu told him to chant the Name keeping count.

436Keeping count, he lovingly chants a hundred thousand names;
from then on detachment from worldly life arose in him.

437Many days after Sri Mahaprabhu's sannyasa
he rendered the nectar of Krishna's lila into the common tongue59.

438The Tenth Canto of the Srimad Bhagavata
he set out in songs in many metres60.

439Taking something from other Puranas as well,
he included it in the Krishna-mangala.

440He named the book Sri Krishna-mangala
and offered it at Sri Chaitanya's feet.

441Sri Krishna Chaitanya showed him favour,
and all the devotees grew fond of him.

442Mahaprabhu commanded Advaita,
"Instruct Madhava in the initiation mantra."

443Sri Advaita Prabhu, at Mahaprabhu's command,
began to speak the mantra into Madhava's ear.

444First he gave him the Hari-nama together with its meaning,
then he spoke the mantra of Radha and Krishna into his ear.

445He instructed him in the kama-gayatri and the kama-bija61
and, explaining the meaning, revealed to him the whole truth.

446From then on Madhava became skilled in bhajana,
and he no longer wished to live in the world.

447Madhava's mother, seeing him indifferent,
was afraid that he would leave home.

448Madhava's mother, to get him married,
in her fear hastily began the preparations.

449Seeing his mother's preparations, Madhava then
ran away and went to Vrindavana.

450Coming to the feet of Sri Rupa, he surrendered himself
and learned the whole truth of bhajana.

451Having taken sannyasa, he stayed in Vrindavana
and performs bhajana in the madhurya-bhava of Vraja.

452Madhava Acharya is the sakhi Sri Madhavi62;
by Sri Rupa's mercy [this awareness] awoke in him.

453Later Madhava became famed as Kavivallabha Acharya63;
all say, "This great-minded one is the Vyasa of the age of Kali."

454He, a great devotee of Krishna, while wandering in Vrindavana,
heard of his mother's death.

455Hearing of his mother's death, he came to Shantipur
and together with Achyuta went to Sri Kheturi.

456Having seen the abhisheka of the sacred deities at Kheturi,
he quickly returned to Vrindavana.

457I went to Vrindavana with the Ishvari
and wandered with great joy together with Madhava Acharya.

458He instructed me in the truth;
to his lotus feet is my special obeisance.

459Now I shall tell of the splendour of the service under Narottama,
seeing which the pashandis were laid low in the dust.

460He built a most excellent temple
and in six chambers installed six deities:

461Gauranga, Vallavikanta, and also Sri Krishna,
Vraja-mohana, Radha-ramana, Radha-kanta — six.

462According to the rules of the service of the eight periods64
he performs the daily service with a joyful heart.

463All year round the sankirtana goes on unceasingly;
seeing it, the pashandis are amazed.

464In one place the Srimad Bhagavata is expounded,
in another the Chaitanya-bhagavata and the Chaitanya-charitamrita are read.

465The Chaitanya-bhagavata used to be called the Chaitanya-mangala;
the mahantas in Vrindavana gave it the name "Bhagavata".

466Seeing that it resembles the Bhagavata,
all gladly call it the Chaitanya-bhagavata.

467In another place many sadhus and mahantas, sitting together,
joyfully converse about Krishna.

468How much shall I tell of the Sri Sankirtana? —
hearing it, the pashandis melted at heart.

469First they sing the Chaitanya-mangala,
after that the Sri Krishna-mangala is sung.

470Then Govinda's songs of the lilas of Gaura and Krishna are sung65;
by Narottama's singing everyone's mind and soul are refreshed.

471Whoever listens to the songs of Vidyapati and Chandidasa on Krishna's lila,
they steal his mind and soul.

472Every year on the day of Sri Phalguna Purnima
there is a great festival at Kheturi.

473All the Vaishnavas come there;
what joy there is cannot be written.

474What my Thakurani did
on the way from Kheturi to Vrindavana66 —

475of how we travelled on the road I now write;
listen, listeners, to the wonders that happened [there].

476I went to Vrindavana with the Thakurani
and saw all the events with my own eyes.

477There was a robber chief named Qutbuddin67;
taking with him many yavanas,

478he came to rob us of our money and the rest —
but cannot find the way and wanders about.

479As they wandered about, the night passed;
seeing the dawn, all were frightened out of their wits.

480In fear all fell at Jahnava's feet:
"Protect us, Mother, we have come to you for refuge!

481We came to rob you of your money and everything,
[but] we wandered and wandered, and the night passed.

482We look in all four directions and see huge snakes:
they are rushing at us to bite.

483Then from somewhere came a voice:
'This Thakurani has subdued you.'

484Hearing this, we were seized with great fear
and, coming to your feet, take refuge."

485Hearing this, the Thakurani, with great joy in her heart,
showed mercy to all the yavanas.

486Then the cry of Hari's name arose there:
all the yavanas dance and sing of Krishna's qualities.

487Hear what happened another day — it is most wonderful:
with the Ishvari we entered a certain village.

488That day we stayed in that village;
the pashandis of the village jeered at us greatly.

489At night they see a dream:
the goddess Chandika in anger speaks these words:

490"You have mocked Jahnava Devi;
for this offence great misfortune will befall you.

491If you take refuge at Jahnava's feet,
then you will be saved; otherwise — ruin."68

492Next morning all the pashandis
came and fell at the Thakurani's feet.

493Jahnava Ishvari, my [mistress], is an ocean of compassion:
she showed them mercy, and all became [her] followers.

494Returning from Vrindavana, Jahnava Ishvari
came to Sri Kheturi and stayed some days.

495With her is always Madhava Acharya69;
by singing and playing he robs everyone of composure70.

496Madhava Acharya is a Varendra brahmana,
a beloved devotee of Nityananda, of the highest [brahmana] lineage71.

497A disciple of Nityananda, he knows none but Nitai
and always meditates on Nitai's feet.

498Nityananda Prabhu has a daughter named Ganga;
Prabhu gave her in marriage to Madhava Acharya.

499Madhava married at the guru's command:
the scriptures say that the guru's command is strongest of all72.

500The greatness of the Lord cannot be understood at all:
by the Lord's will the impossible comes to pass.

501Think no ill of a marriage between Radhi and Varendra:
Radhi and Varendra are the offspring of the same ancestors73.

502There have been many marriages between Radhi and Varendra;
the difference of names is only from the difference of regions.

503Five twice-born came to the sacrifice of Adishura;
their descendants are the Radhi and Varendra communities74.

504Madhava Acharya, having married Ganga,
by the guru's command became a Radhi75.

505Madhava Acharya is called Shantanu:
this Ganga Devi is the Ganga herself, become water76.

506I learned to play instruments from Madhava Acharya:
in his mercy he taught me to play.

507At his lotus feet are my countless obeisances;
how much mercy he showed me has no limit.

508When Phalguna Purnima drew near,
the festival at Sri Kheturi began.

509Little by little all the mahantas came;
how many people came cannot be counted.

510All came — Srinivasa, Shyamananda;
Virachandra and Achyutananda came with many Vaishnavas.

511On the day of the full moon in the morning there was nama-sankirtana;
they performed the abhisheka of the deities and sprinkled them with coloured powder.

512All the devotees, sprinkling powder on the bodies of the deities,
gladly sprinkle powder on one another.

513Having played with the powder, all took prasada;
having seen the evening arati, they began the kirtana.

514First, Vasu Ghosha's songs of Gaura's lila:
whoever hears them, his heart melts and tears flow.

515Devidasa and Madhava Acharya play the mridanga,
Gauranga [Dasa] and Govinda Dasa play the karatalas.

516Santosha, Govinda, Gokula — all sing songs;
Krishna's lila in the songs of Chandidasa captivates everyone's heart.

517Achyutananda, Virabhadra and Srinivasa,
Shyamananda, Narottama, Ramachandra Dasa,

518with arms raised, dance and sing of Krishna's lila;
what joy there was cannot be written.

519Drawn by the power of Narottama's bhakti and his song,
Krishna could not hold back and came together with his Beloved.

520In all ten directions water and land were lit up;
a spotless radiance, like lightning in a cloud.

521Then all saw the form of Radha and Krishna;
what joy they felt cannot be told.

522A fragrant breeze blew, wonderful indeed;
anklets and belts of little bells tinkled sweetly.

523Above the sankirtana, in the vault of the sky,
Bhagavan appeared and vanished.

524Narottama fell to the ground senseless;
Ramachandra and the others weep, rolling on the ground.

525Sri Krishna's lila cannot be understood at all;
by Krishna's will all grew calm.

526A cry rose in the sky: "Blessed is Narottama!"
All embrace one another and bow.

527Narottama is an avesha-avatara of Bhagavan;
by his mercy we were delivered.

528Narottama's bhajana and his sport are supremely excellent;
in his mercy he delivers all people.

529One day Narottama, fixing his mind,
contemplates the rasa-lila of Radha and Krishna.

530He remains in samadhi, his body motionless;
friends, kinsfolk and devotees, seeing this, grew alarmed77.

531Ramachandra says, "Do not worry at all:
when the samadhi breaks, he will regain consciousness."

532Two days passed, and all were in distress;
Srinivasa Acharya came and calmed everyone.

533Srinivasa Acharya with effort brought him to consciousness;
then the cry arose: "Hari! Hari! Hari!"

534Regaining outer consciousness, Narottama bowed to the Acharya,
and Srinivasa Acharya embraced him.

535Listen, listen, listeners, with one mind:
now I shall describe the deliverance of a pashandi.

536In Gopalpur lived a Vedic brahmana;
he taught pupils and knew many shastras.

537His name was Gurudasa Bhattacharya;
this wicked man reviled Narottama in every way.

538From his reviling he was struck with leprosy;
neither propitiatory rites nor treatment rid him of the disease.

539He constantly meditates on Bhavani:
"For what offence has such misery befallen me?"

540At night Bhavani showed herself to him in a dream:
"You suffer so for reviling Narottama.

541You have always regarded Narottama as a shudra —
for this offence you are suffering greatly.

542Narottama is the embodiment of Sri Chaitanya's prema;
whoever looks on him with bhakti, the distress of his mind departs.

543He is an avesha-avatara of Nityananda Prabhu;
in his mercy he will deliver the world.

544The sinner who regards Narottama as an ordinary man
sinks into hell after death.

545The wretch who calls Narottama a shudra
goes to hell with his whole family, there is no doubt.

546Whoever is devoted to Vishnu
has the sacred thread within his heart, know this for certain.

547A devotee of Krishna is greater than a brahmana;
a brahmana without devotion to Krishna is truly the lowest of shudras.

548Thus it is said:
*'Even a chandala devoted to Vishnu is the best of the twice-born;
but one without devotion to Vishnu, though twice-born, is lower than a dog-eater.'*78

549Having said this, Bhagavati vanished;
waking, the brahmana sees that the night has passed.

550In the morning the brahmana, coming from there to Kheturi,
prostrated himself at Narottama's feet.

551He related his dream in detail:
"Have mercy, Prabhu, give me the boat of your feet.

552There is none in the world, Prabhu, as low as I;
if you deliver me, your fame will spread everywhere."

553Hearing this, Narottama in mercy placed his foot on his head;
he was freed from the disease — all saw it.

554Thakura Mahashaya is an ocean of compassion:
in his pity he made him his servant.

555From then on many people, fearful at heart,
came and took refuge at Narottama's feet.

556There was a Vedic brahmana named Jagannatha Acharya,
a great pandita, a resident of Budhari.

557Seeing that [Narottama] was initiating brahmanas, this brahmana Jagannatha
became furious with Narottama79.

558[Wishing] to enter into debate with Sri Narottama,
he began inwardly to meditate on the feet of Kali.

559At night Jagannatha saw a dream:
Narottama is an avesha of Sri Bhagavan.

560Greatly afraid at heart, Jagannatha
quickly came to the village of Sri Kheturi.

561He came and took refuge at Narottama's feet,
and Narottama in his mercy gave him the initiation mantra.

562Narottama made many brahmanas his disciples —
and the pashandi brahmanas all burned [with spite] like fire.

563Wicked brahmanas, robber chiefs from Bengal,
were delivered by the mercy of Thakura Mahashaya.

564I shall give the names of some of them;
listen, listen, listeners, with one mind.

565Govinda Banerji and Lalita Ghoshal,
Kalidasa Chatterji, a most wicked robber,

566Nilamani Mukhuti and Ramajaya Chakravarti,
Harinatha Ganguli and Shiva Chakravarti80.

567Formerly they were soldiers of Chand Raya
and committed much robbery together with Chand Raya.

568They are Chand Raya's kinsmen and friends;
fighting, they defeated the yavanas.

569They plundered many lands and extended their domain;
out of fear the yavana king did not advance against them.

570On the day when Chand Raya was taken captive,
all of them fled in fear.

571Knowing Thakura Mahashaya's power and its essence,
all became [his] disciples, giving up their former trade81.

572[Narottama] has a kinsman, Raja Narasimha Raya;
he lives very far away, at Pakkapalli82.

573His city on the bank of the Ganga is most delightful;
he cares for his subjects with love, as for his sons.

574Many brahmana panditas live near him;
once, by fate, a great pandita came there.

575The pandita's name was Rupa Narayana;
nowhere had he been defeated in debate.

576His life is supremely sweet;
I heard much of it from Narasimha Raya.

577I shall describe something of it here in brief —
hearing of his life, all will be very glad.

578In Bengal there was the kingdom of Kamarupa, very pure;
the Pathans took it after a great war.

579The capital of that country is Egarasindur,
a most beautiful [town] on the bank of the Brahmaputra.

580Egarasindur and Mirjafarpur,
Dagdaga, Kutishvara and Hosenpur —

581all these places lie on the bank of the Brahmaputra;
people from various lands trade there.

582Egarasindur and Dagdaga
are famous for trade — everyone knows it.

583Merchants from all quarters live here;
all buy and sell with joyful hearts.

584Near Egarasindur there is a village
named Bhitadiya, where kulinas live.

585There lives the brahmana Lakshminatha Lahiri;
his virtuous wife is Kamala Devi, exceedingly beautiful.

586He is a Varendra brahmana, foremost among the kulinas,
honoured by all brahmanas, revered everywhere.

587A son was born to him, like Indra himself;
they named him Sri Rupachandra.

588As a child Rupachandra was very naughty
and even at his father's bidding did not learn to read and write.

589However hard Lakshminatha Lahiri tried,
he would by no means study.

590One day his father in anger threw ashes on his rice;
in distress he got up and left without eating.

591Bowing to his mother, he left home
and in a few days reached the village of Panditbari83.

592Having studied grammar, he received the title Chakravarti;
his fame grew from his studies at Navadvipa.

593Having studied many shastras, he became very learned
and gained fame as an Acharya.

594From there he went to Nilachala
and saw Mahaprabhu in the sankirtana.

595Bowing to Sri Chaitanya from afar,
he joyfully beheld Jagannatha.

596From there he went to the city of Puna in Maharashtra
to study the Vedas and the rest, with a glad heart.

597Rupachandra had a great memory for what he heard;
he studied the Vedas, the Vedangas, the Vedanta — everything.

598Seeing his profound learning in many shastras,
the teachers gave him the title Sarasvati.

599Making a digvijaya, he goes to various places84:
wherever he sees a pandita, he defeats him in debate.

600Having wandered through many places, he came to Vrindavana
and hears that two supreme panditas live there —

601two Gosanis named Rupa and Sanatana:
in no land are there panditas equal to these two.

602Rupachandra came to the two Gosanis,
boundlessly glad that he would debate.

603Coming, he bowed to the Gosvamis;
the Gosanis respectfully gave him a seat.

604Asking after his welfare, they say, "Why have you come?"
Rupachandra says, "I have come for a debate.

605I have studied many shastras and become a pandita;
a debate with the two of you is what I desire."

606The Gosvamis say, "What fruit comes of debate?"
The pandita says, "A test in the shastras, victory and defeat."

607The Gosanis say, "There is no need for debate:
we both accept defeat."

608Aggrieved, Rupachandra rose from there:
"The Gosvamis would not debate with me out of fear,"

609saying this, he goes towards the bank of the Yamuna;
on the way he met Sri Jiva Gosvami.

610Sri Jiva, questioning him, learned everything,
and [Rupachandra] in anger began the debate right there.

611Sri Jiva said, "Rupa and Sanatana are my teachers;
if you defeat me, I shall call you the victor."

612Jiva said, "The two Gosanis are supreme panditas;
if you debate with me, this will become clear to you."

613The debate between Jiva and Rupachandra went on for five days;
who won and who lost could not be known.

614On the seventh day the debate went on for a long time:
Jiva was victorious, and Rupachandra was crushed.

615Sri Jiva, refuting Rupachandra's advaita-vada,
established dvaita-vada with reasons and proofs.

616He showed the pre-eminence of the Vaishnava teaching:
bhakti was acknowledged above jnana, karma and yoga.

617The defeated Rupachandra, at Sri Jiva's feet,
prostrated himself gladly.

618With joined palms he offers praise to Sri Jiva:
"By your mercy my mind has been purified."

619Sri Jiva in his mercy placed his foot on his head,
embraced him and seated him beside himself.

620Rupa said, "Prabhu, you have shown me mercy:
you have dispelled all my darkness of ignorance.

621I have committed countless offences against you;
have mercy, purify my wicked mind."

622Jiva said, "Before me you bear no offence:
it is Chaitanya Gosani who has shown you mercy."

623Hearing this, Rupachandra, touching his head
to Sri Jiva's feet, sheds tears of prema.

624Rupachandra said, "Prabhu, Sri Jiva Gosani,
my offences have no end.

625How much tamas I showed
before Sri Rupa and Sanatana Gosvami cannot be told.

626Remembering it, my heart burns;
I see no way out, Prabhu, I see no way out!"

627Having said this, Rupachandra lamented bitterly;
Sri Jiva Gosvami carefully consoled him.

628Sri Jiva Gosvami, taking Sri Rupachandra with him,
gladly goes to the Gosvamis.

629Rupachandra at the feet of Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana
falls to the ground and rolls in great sorrow:

630"There is no sinner in the three worlds as low as I;
my offences cannot be counted.

631Drunk with tamas, with a mind gripped by delusion,
I came to debate with you.

632Forgive my offences, Prabhu, have mercy on this low one,
deliver the fallen, give the shade of your feet.

633By the mercy of Sri Jiva Gosvami I have gained a little knowledge;
by the strength of his mercy I have beheld your feet."

634Saying this and much else, Rupa rolls on the ground;
in distress he weeps, his heart groans.

635Seeing Rupachandra's humility, Rupa and Sanatana
in their mercy placed their feet on his head.

636Rupa and Sanatana said to Rupachandra,
"You bear no offence; your mind has become pure.

637Sri Krishna Chaitanyachandra has shown you mercy;
you have become blessed in all the world."

638Having said this, the two Gosanis embraced him;
tears of prema flowed from his eyes.

639Rupachandra humbly says to the Gosvamis,
"Have mercy, give this low one initiation into [the mantra of] Krishna."

640Hearing this, both Gosvamis pondered;
at that moment a voice rose in the sky:

641"Give Rupachandra the Hari-nama, both of you;
initiation into the Gopala mantra he will receive from Narottama."

642Hearing the voice from the sky, the two Gosvamis
speak into his ear the maha-mantra of the Hari-nama:

643"Keeping count, you will always chant the Hari-nama;
initiation into [the mantra of] Krishna you will receive from Narottama.

644In the village of Sri Kheturi at Gopalpur, in the land of Garerhat,
Narottama has been born — so we tell you85.

645At twelve years of age he will come to Vrindavana
and become a disciple of Lokanatha Gosani, a treasury of virtues."

646Having said this, Sanatana fell silent;
Rupachandra touched his head to the Gosvamis' feet.

647At that very moment a wonder took place:
Narayana entered into Rupachandra.

648Rupa and Sanatana, seeing the power of his bhakti,
embraced him and felt prema.

649The Gosanis said, "Narayana has entered your body;
from today your name is Rupa Narayana."

650Having said this, they infused shakti into him,
and Rupa Narayana bowed at the Gosanis' feet.

651For some time he lived in Vrindavana
and studied the shastras of bhakti under Sri Jiva.

652He studies the Bhagavata with the commentaries of the Svami and the Toshani86,
gladly studies the Laghu- and Brihad-bhagavatamrita,

653studies the [Bhakti-]rasamrita, the Ujjvala, all the Sandarbhas;
studying the dramas and the rest, he found great delight.

654Having seen the whole of the Mathura-mandala,
immersed in bliss, he performs nama-sankirtana.

655To Sri Rupa, Sanatana, Raghunatha Bhatta,
Sri Jiva, Gopala Bhatta, the devotee Kashinatha,

656and to the two Gosanis, Lokanatha and Bhugarbha,
he bowed with great joy in his heart.

657To Brahmachari Krishnadasa and Kashishvara —
he bowed at the feet of all the Vaishnavas.

658All the Vaishnavas showed him favour;
taking leave, he went to Nilachala.

659There he heard of Mahaprabhu's disappearance;
in great grief he lost consciousness.

660By Prabhu's will sleep overcame him,
and in a dream Gaurachandra appeared to him.

661Prabhu said, "Listen, Rupa Narayana:
you will meet Narasimha Raya.

662Staying with him, you will receive from Narottama
the Gopala mantra together with him."

663Having said this, Gaura placed his feet on his head
and, showing him favour, went away.

664Having seen the dream, Rupa Narayana
woke, sat up and sheds tears of prema.

665By Prabhu's will he found peace
and came to the house of Gadadhara Pandita.

666Bowing, he related everything,
and Gadadhara placed his feet on his head.

667Then he went to Sri Svarupa Gosvami
and humbly told him everything.

668He bowed at Svarupa's feet,
and Svarupa in his mercy placed his foot on his head.

669Showing him favour, he infused shakti into him
and told him many hidden truths.

670He bowed to Sri Dasa Gosvami,
and he showed him boundless favour.

671With joy in his heart he beheld Sri Jagannatha
and freely offered praises of his own composing.

672Bowing, he left that place,
and on the way he met Ramananda.

673Learning who he was, he bowed to the Raya,
and Raya Ramananda showed him favour.

674Having thus met all the devotees of Gaura,
after some time he came to the land of Gauda.

675For some days he wandered through various places —
and heard that Nityananda Prabhu had disappeared.

676Hearing of his disappearance, he grieved greatly,
and in a dream Nityananda appeared to him.

677Seeing Prabhu, he fainted with bliss;
[Prabhu] placed his foot on his head, and his heart grew calm.

678Nitai said, "Listen, O Rupa Narayana:
soon you will meet Narasimha.

679For some time you will stay here,
and after some days you will see Narottama."

680Having said this, Nityananda vanished;
waking, he sees that night has turned to morning.

681What joy he felt on seeing Prabhu cannot be described;
what grief at losing sight of him cannot be written.

682By Prabhu's will he recovered somewhat;
and some days later he heard of Advaita Prabhu's departure.

683He grieved greatly, and in a dream he had darshana:
Prabhu said, "You will meet Raja Narasimha."

684Having said this, Prabhu placed his foot on his head
and, showing him favour, went away.

685Waking, Rupa Narayana was filled with grief;
after some time the night turned to dawn.

686By Prabhu's will he recovered somewhat
and, having done his morning duties, went to bathe in the Ganga.

687To that same ghat a raja came,
with many brahmana panditas and countless people.

688He learned from people that this was Narasimha Raya;
he bathed in the Ganga with a joyful heart.

689Raja Narasimha, seeing Rupa Narayana,
came up to him and asked who he was.

690Rupa Narayana was exceedingly handsome;
deep reverence arose in Narasimha's heart.

691Raja Narasimha Raya with great insistence
took Rupa Narayana to his own palace.

692Many brahmana panditas came to the palace,
and Rupa Narayana defeated them all in debate.

693Rupa Narayana's fame spread everywhere:
in no land is there a pandita equal to him.

694The raja loves Rupa Narayana dearly;
by his counsel the raja's fame grows greatly.

695Rupa Narayana knows the yoga-shastra deeply;
I myself studied some yoga-shastra with him.

696Certain kinds of yoga I learned from him,
and I honoured him as my guru in yoga.

697To write of his life is the Ishvari's command;
I have written briefly and shall not write in detail.

698One day Narasimha, together with Rupa Narayana,
was sitting in assembly with his courtiers.

699At that time some brahmana panditas came,
distressed: "Ruin has come!

700Narottama Dasa, the son of Krishnananda Datta87,
by giving the mantra to brahmanas has ruined everything.

701It seems the dreadful [age of] Kali has now arrived:
hearing that a shudra has brahmana disciples, we tremble.

702From somewhere he brought and spread the Vaishnava teaching
and abolished the worship of all the gods and goddesses.

703There are no more sacrifices, no slaying of animals88;
he has ruined the country, the rites have gone to waste.

704Giving up fish and meat, they eat only vegetable food;
in the sankirtana they dance and weep like madmen.

705All the Vedic and Tantric rites have vanished;
with the sankirtana he has beguiled all the people.

706What sorcery does this Narottama Dasa know? —
many learned brahmanas have become his disciples.

707Protect the caste of brahmanas, Mahashaya:
lead us all to his house.

708We shall defeat him in a debate on the shastras —
and he will flee in fear."

709Hearing this, Narasimha Raya said to Rupa Narayana,
"What do you say, brother? Speak now."89

710Rupa Narayana said, "Listen, Maharaja:
go with your whole retinue, do not delay.

711It seems our good fortune has dawned at last:
Thakura Mahashaya has drawn [us] by his virtues."90

712Rupa Narayana said to the brahmana panditas,
"Let us go with your pupils; we shall defeat Narottama in debate."91

713But inwardly Rupa says, "Such is the greatness [of his] I have heard of —
by the Mahashaya's mercy all people will be delivered."

714Taking the teachers and Rupa Narayana with him,
the Raya set out for Kheturi.

715Near Kheturi, in the village of Kumarpur,
the Raya one day stopped to rest.

716Meanwhile Thakura Mahashaya heard all about it:
Narasimha Raya had come with many panditas.

717Ramachandra Kaviraja said to Narottama,
"We shall go in disguise and defeat them there."

718Having said this, they took the Mahashaya's permission
and gladly went to Kumarpur.

719Ramachandra, Govinda and Ganganarayana,
Harihara, Ramakrishna, Jagannatha — these few

720dressed up as an oilman, a liquor-seller, a barui and a potter92
and, taking various goods, set up a market there.

721Some pupils came to buy goods;
when they asked the price, they were answered in Sanskrit.

722The pupils haughtily spoke in Sanskrit —
and after a little conversation all were defeated.

723The oilman and the liquor-seller say, "Fools, what do you know?
If you have any shame, bring your teachers."

724Ashamed, the pupils say to their teachers,
"An oilman, a liquor-seller, a barui and a potter have defeated us all.

725We asked, 'Where did you learn the shastras?' —
and they told us everything in detail:

726'We keep shops at the holy seat of Kheturi93;
the shastras are much studied there — we have retained a little.'"

727Hearing this, the teachers flared up like fire,
and all went to the market to debate.

728For a long time all debated —
and the panditas were utterly defeated.

729The panditas came to the raja's camp
and told him how they had been defeated.

730The panditas say, "We shall go no further to Kheturi;
come, let us quickly flee from here."

731Rupa Narayana said, "There is nothing to worry about:
Narottama Gosani will show mercy to all.

732What is the use of fleeing?
Take refuge at Narottama's feet.

733All the shastras say that the Vaishnava dharma is the highest dharma;
becoming Vaishnavas, people attain bhakti and liberation.

734Thus it is said:
*'The Vaishnava is the highest dharma, the Vaishnava is the highest austerity,
the Vaishnava is the highest object of worship, the Vaishnava is the highest guru.'*

735*'Let one seek health from the Sun, wealth from Fire,
knowledge from Shankara, and liberation from Janardana.'*94"

736Meanwhile all the traders from the market,
calling the pupils, gave them the goods.

737They said, "We make our profit in various places;
[this] we all give to the brahmanas."

738Having said this and handed over the goods,
the traders went off to their own places.

739Meanwhile all ate and went to sleep;
towards morning the panditas saw a dream:

740Bhagavati, sword in hand and with an angry face, says,
"You have reviled Narottama, you wicked ones!

741You studied, yet nothing was born in you;
by reviling a Vaishnava you have fallen into the abyss.

742Even if I hack your heads to pieces,
the grief of my heart will not end.

743Narottama is an avesha-avatara of the Lord95;
in his heart is a dazzlingly radiant sacred thread.

744He in whose heart is Brahman is a brahmana;
the outer thread is only the mark of the brahmana caste.

745Tomorrow you will take initiation from Narottama;
if Narottama shows you favour, you are saved."

746Having said this, Bhagavati vanished,
and all the teachers woke and sat up.

747Having seen the dream, they tremble with fear, utterly subdued,
and told the dream to the raja in detail.

748The raja said, "Before, you did not heed the warning
and regarded Narottama as an ordinary man.

749What he does is beyond the power of men:
Sri Thakura Mahashaya is worshipped by the gods."

750Having said this, he calmed the teachers,
and all, having bathed and so on, went to Kheturi.

751They bowed to the deities, rolling on the ground,
and prostrated themselves before Narottama:

752"There is no sinner in the world as low as we are;
forgive our offences, have mercy, Gosani."

753Narottama, showing great mercy to all,
lifted his foot and placed it on their heads.

754Then he gave all the brahmanas initiation into [the mantra of] Krishna;
what mercy he showed cannot be told.

755Those of them who were the chief panditas —
I shall now proclaim their names:

756Yadunatha Vidyabhushana and Kashinatha96,
known everywhere by the title Tarka-bhushana;

757Haridasa Shiromani and Chandrakanta,
known everywhere by the title Nyaya-panchanana;

758Shivacharana and Durgadasa — these two,
whom all call by the titles Vidya-vagisha and Vidyaratna97.

759The names of the panditas I have written here,
but the names of the pupils I could not write.

760Meanwhile Raja Narasimha and Rupa Narayana,
having bowed to the six deities and offered them praise,

761came to Narottama's feet and prostrated themselves;
what humility they showed cannot be described.

762Narottama, showing favour to both98,
lifted his foot and placed it on their heads.

763Learning who Raja Narasimha was,
in great mercy he gave him the mantra of Krishna.

764Then Narasimha Raya told Thakura Mahashaya
in detail who Rupa Narayana was:

765what had happened in Vrindavana,
and how they had met him —

766all this he described in detail;
hearing it, Ramachandra and the others were glad.

767Hearing it, Thakura Mahashaya in his mercy
gave him the Hari-nama with its meaning into his ear,

768gave the ten-syllable Gopala mantra,
and then gave the kama-gayatri and the kama-bija.

769Rupa Narayana, prostrating himself,
placed the Mahashaya's feet on his head.

770Then he bowed to Ramachandra and the others;
what joy there was cannot be described.

771Having seen the rajabhoga and the arati99,
all gladly ate prasada.

772Sri Thakura Mahashaya, having eaten prasada,
had the remnants from his plate distributed to the disciples.

773On another day Narasimha brought his wife,
and Narottama Gosani gave her the mantra.

774Listen, listeners, to the story of yet another day;
I shall describe what took place.

775One day two brahmanas, having seen a dream,
came gladly to Narottama.

776Bowing, both say, "We have seen a dream
that we took the sacred mantra from you."

777Hearing this, Narottama gave both the mantra of Krishna,
and both brahmanas were utterly overwhelmed with prema.

778They are two brothers, Radhi brahmanas of the Savarna gotra:
Sri Balarama and Rupa Narayana100.

779The prema-bhakti of both is extraordinary;
their home is in the village of Sri Kheturi.

780Narottama, seeing the prema-bhakti of both,
appointed them to the service of the sacred deities.

781Both are qualified for the bhajana of Sri Krishna;
at Kheturi everyone calls them Pujari.

782Their zeal in bhajana cannot be described;
great is Narottama Thakura's mercy upon them.

783Narottama Thakura's disciples are countless;
in describing the branches I shall give only a general indication.

784I shall describe yet another day,
by hearing of which sins are destroyed.

785Little by little Sri Phalguna Purnima came,
and all the mahantas came here.

786To subdue all the pashandis,
[the Prabhus] displayed one great wonder of power101.

787On the third day after Sri Phalguna Purnima
they held a great assembly with delight in their hearts.

788A great many people gathered at the assembly;
I shall record the names of Chaitanya's companions.

789Shyamananda came with Rasika and other devotees;
full of enthusiasm came Hridaya Chaitanya and others;

790Achyutananda, Krishna Mishra, Gopala, Yadava,
Shyamadasa, Yadunatha, Madhava Acharya and all the rest;

791Vasudha, Jahnava, Ganga and Virachandra,
Madhava Acharya and others, and Sundarananda;

792with Yadunandana and others, Sri Raghunandana,
Sridasa, Gokulananda and Sulochana;

793Raja Vira Hambira, Krishnavallabha, Vyasa —
all came to Kheturi, and Srinivasa too.

794A great many people gathered at the assembly;
a great many pashandis also entered the assembly.

795Srinivasa expounded the Srimad Bhagavata,
and Virabhadra Gosvami delivered a discourse102:

796the Vaishnava dharma is greater than all dharmas —
take up this dharma, all of you, making your minds firm.

797Thus it is said:
*"Ganapatya, and likewise Saura, Shaiva, Shakta, in order;
of all these dharmas the Vaishnava [is held to be] the chief."*

798*"The Vaishnava is the highest dharma, the Vaishnava is the highest austerity,
the Vaishnava is the highest object of worship, the Vaishnava is the highest guru."*103

799Never, brothers, take a non-Vaishnava as guru;
leave such a guru and serve a Vaishnava Gosani.

800The mantra of Krishna surpasses all mantras;
take this mantra, all of you, and become foremost among men.

801Thus in the Gautamiya[-tantra]:
*"Among the mantras of the Ganapatyas, Sauras, Shaivas and Shaktas, O keeper of vows,
and among all the Vaishnava ones, the mantras of Krishna yield the greatest fruit."*

802This mantra should be taken from a Vaishnava belonging to a sampradaya,
and the mantra of one outside a sampradaya should be rejected.

803Thus in the Gautamiya[-tantra]:
*"For those instructed through a sampradaya perfection will surely come;
but mantras outside a sampradaya are held to be fruitless."*

804And in the Padma[-purana]:
*"Therefore in the age of Kali there will be four [founders of] sampradayas —
Sri, Brahma, Rudra and Sanaka: Vaishnavas who purify the earth."*

805*"Mantras that are outside a sampradaya are held to be fruitless:
they bring no perfection by sadhana even in hundreds of millions of kalpas."*104

806A mantra [that has come] from Krishna through the succession of gurus —
that is what the panditas call a mantra of the sampradaya.

807But a mantra of Krishna received from a non-Vaishnava
is everywhere known as a mantra outside the sampradaya.

808Ganapatyas, Sauras, Shaktas, Shaivas,
offenders and the like — all are called non-Vaishnavas.

809Whoever has received the mantra of Krishna from a non-Vaishnava
certainly goes to hell.

810Therefore, obeying the command of the shastras,
one should take the sacred mantra anew from a Vaishnava.
