811Thus in the Hari-bhakti-vilasa, [in the section] on the greatness of the guru:
*"With a mantra given by a non-Vaishnava one goes to hell;
let him therefore receive it again, properly and according to the rules, from a Vaishnava guru."*

812Whoever has received the mantra of Krishna is called a Vaishnava;
a devotee of Vishnu is certainly greater than a brahmana.

813Thus in the Hari-bhakti-vilasa:
*"A man who has received initiation into [the mantra of] Vishnu and is devoted to Vishnu's service
is called a Vaishnava by the knowing; any other is a non-Vaishnava."*

814And elsewhere:
*"One who is devoted to the Hari-nama, intent on the worship of Krishna,
who receives the mantra of Krishna and knows Vishnu — he is a Vaishnava."*

815*"Even a chandala devoted to Vishnu is the best of the twice-born;
but one without devotion to Vishnu, though twice-born, is lower than a dog-eater."*

816In the Bhakti-sandarbha:
*"Even a dog-eater, O lord of the earth, if he is a devotee of Vishnu, is higher than a twice-born;
but one without devotion to Vishnu, even a sannyasi, is lower than a dog-eater."*

817One who is devoted to Krishna is not a shudra;
a twice-born without devotion to Krishna is called the lowest of shudras.

818Thus it is said:
*"The devotees of Bhagavan are not shudras: they are the best of Bhagavatas;
the shudras in all varnas are those who are not devoted to Janardana."*

819As bronze by the action of rasa attains the nature of gold,
so a man by initiation from Krishna attains twice-born status.

820Thus in the Hari-bhakti-vilasa, [in the section] on the greatness of initiation:
*"As bronze by the rules of [alchemical] treatment becomes gold,
so by the rules of initiation twice-born status arises in men."*105

821This Narottama is born of a Kayastha family;
some, calling him a shudra, treat him with contempt.

822A devotee of Krishna is greater than a brahmana:
whoever knows the shastras firmly accepts this.

823Attaining twice-born status through initiation from Krishna is the word of the shastras; whoever disbelieves this goes to the abode of hell.

824He who is called Brahman, Paramatma, Bhagavan —
that Supreme Lord is Krishna, know this for certain.

825One in whom Krishna always dwells within and without —
he is a brahmana, I say with certainty.

826The thread on a brahmana's neck all people see,
but the thread in the heart of a sadhaka is always hidden.

827Whoever, tearing open his breast, shows the sacred thread —
him I count among the brahmanas.

828Narottama is the embodiment of Mahaprabhu's prema,
an avesha-avatara of Nityananda Prabhu.

829He is a part of Nityananda; honour him as the Lord;
tearing open his breast, he will show the sacred thread."

830Having said this, Virachandra fell silent
and bade [Narottama] show the sacred thread to all.

831As in olden times Hanuman in the assembly,
tearing open his breast, showed Sita and Rama106 —

832so Narottama Gosani, at the bidding of the assembly,
tearing open his breast, showed the sacred thread.

833The shining thread is like a ray of the sun;
the pashandis cannot bear to look at it.

834Whoever is a devotee looks on with delight in his heart;
seeing it, the pashandis tremble all over in great terror.

835The devotees and all the pashandis,
bowing, offer him many praises.

836Then Narottama, hiding the thread,
showed the pashandis great mercy.

837Then cries arose: "Blessed! Blessed! Blessed!"
All embraced one another.

838Narottama bowed to the companions of Gaura
and, taking their permission, began the sankirtana.

839Having sung for a while, they rest;
Narasimha and Rupa Narayana came and bowed.

840Then Rupa Narayana began to sing,
and Narasimha Raya hung the khol on his shoulder.

841What singing, what playing, what a sweet voice! —
everyone's heart melted beyond measure107.

842With his sweet voice he captivated the hearts of the assembly,
and all, raising their arms, began to dance.

843Prabhu Virabhadra, firmly embracing
Sri Rupa Narayana, dances.

844Then Rupa Narayana fell at Prabhu's feet,
and Virachandra in his mercy placed his foot on his head.

845What joy there was cannot be written;
after a while the sankirtana came to an end.

846Prabhu Virabhadra, the abode of all virtues,
asked Rupa Narayana who he was.

847He learned the whole story from beginning to end
and was convinced that this was the shakti of Sri Rupa.

848Virachandra said, "Listen, Rupa Narayana:
your bhakti has melted my heart.

849You are the shakti of Sri Rupa Gosvami;
I bestow on you the title 'Gosvami'."

850Hearing this, Rupa Narayana rejoiced
and clasped the Gosvami's feet with both hands.

851Achyutananda, Krishna Mishra and Sri Gopala,
Srinivasa, Shyamananda and Raghunandana,

852Ramachandra, Santosha Datta, Sri Gokulananda,
Vasudha, Jahnava, Ganga and Sri Govinda —

853all the companions of Gauranga — how many shall I name? —
all showed him fitting favour.

854Rupa Narayana bowed at the feet of all,
and all embraced him with love.

855The mahantas took leave and went to their own places,
and Rupa Narayana stayed here for some time.

856One day Sri Rupa Narayana
asked the Mahashaya for his siddha name.

857Thakura Mahashaya, showing him favour,
gave him the siddha name "Sri Narayani Manjari".

858The greatness of Narottama Thakura is boundless;
what can I, wretched and without bhakti, know how to write?

859My Thakurani in Sri Vrindavana
had promised to send a sacred image.

860She had an image of Sri Radha made for Madanamohana108
and sent it to Vrindavana.

861Seeing it, the Gosvamis were filled with great joy
and placed Sri Radha to the left of Sri Madanamohana.

862The Ishvari's story I do not write further here:
I have described it in detail in the Virachandra-charita109.

863My Sri Thakurani had eight sons;
seven gave up their lives at the obeisance of Abhirama110.

864The last son is Virabhadra, named Virachandra;
I have recorded his story in the Virachandra-charita.

865At Srikhanda, at the memorial festival of Narahari,
all came and performed a great sankirtana.

866At that time a blind man named Ramai
came to see the kirtana and the dancing111.

867He hears the singing but cannot see the dancing at all;
clutching both his eyes, he only cries, "Alas! Alas!

868I cannot see the dancing in Krishna's sankirtana:
for what offence have my eyes been taken from me?"

869Saying this, he weeps bitterly;
Prabhu Virachandra gave him sight.

870Holding his eyes, Prabhu said, "Look, Ramai:
in this sankirtana everyone is dancing."

871Having received his sight, Ramai fell at Prabhu's feet,
and Prabhu placed his foot on his head.

872Then cries of "Blessed! Blessed!" rose in the sky;
all embrace one another with love.

873How Prabhu in his compassion gave him sight
I have written in detail in the Virachandra-charita.

874My Prabhu Virachandra is a merciful Gosani;
there is no end to the disciples he made.

875In the village of Kadra there is a certain Jayagopala;
for disregarding the guru's grace he excommunicated him112.

876To Srinivasa and all the mahantas
Virabhadra made it known by letter.

877Here I have written a little, in brief;
in the Virachandra-charita I have described it in detail.

878One day Virachandra, with his mother's leave,
set out for Nilachala with a joyful heart.

879Going there, he beheld Jagannatha
and saw all the places of Mahaprabhu's lila.

880Meeting all of Prabhu's companions who were there,
he came to Gopivallabhapur113.

881Having met Shyamananda there,
after some time he arrived at Khardaha.

882Here I have told a little, in brief;
I have described it in detail in the Virachandra-charita.

883Having stayed some time at Khardaha, my Prabhu
set out for Vrindavana with a happy heart.

884From Khardaha by way of Ambika and Shantipur
he came with a joyful heart to Navadvipa.

885Having seen the places of Mahaprabhu's lila,
he went by way of Khanda to Yajigrama.

886Staying there two to four days,
he went by way of Katwa and Budhari to Kheturi.

887Staying some time in the village of Sri Kheturi,
after some days he arrived in Vrindavana.

888Here I have described nothing of what happened on the way:
I have told it in detail in Prabhu's life.

889He met the Gosvamis
and toured the whole Mathura-mandala.

890All this I have recorded in great detail
and with joy in the Virachandra-charita114.

891Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana,
Radha-Damodara and Sri Radha-ramana,

892Radha-vinoda and others he beheld;
what joy Prabhu felt cannot be written.

893All that concerns these deities —
how each of them was found — setting it out clearly,

894I have recorded in detail in the Virachandra-charita;
whoever hears it, his heart melts.

895My Prabhu Virachandra, from Vrindavana,
after some days came to Sri Ekachakra.

896He beheld the place of Ekachakra,
where Nityananda Prabhu was born.

897Seeing the places of Nitai's childhood lilas,
with a joyful heart he shed streams of prema from his eyes.

898This I have described in detail in the Virachandra-charita;
from there my Prabhu came to Kheturi.

899Seeing him, Narottama fell at Prabhu's feet,
and Prabhu embraced him with great delight.

900Having beheld the sacred deities, Prabhu
performed nama-sankirtana for some time.

901Having eaten prasada, Prabhu together with Narottama
spoke for some time of what had happened in Vrindavana.

902Hearing the blessing of Lokanatha Gosvami,
Narottama shed tears from both his eyes.

903Staying some time at Sri Kheturi,
he set out from there for Yajigrama.

904The Acharya, hearing of Virachandra's arrival,
came out to meet him and brought him to his own house.

905Srinivasa bowed at Virachandra's feet,
and Prabhu Virachandra embraced him.

906The Ishvari and Gauranga-priya were there too;
they came and bowed at Prabhu's feet115.

907Telling of his journey to Vrindavana,
he conveyed the blessing of Sri Bhatta Gosvami.

908Hearing the blessing of his own Prabhu, Srinivasa —
who had not [again] seen his holy feet — heaves deep sighs.

909Staying some time at Yajigrama, Prabhu
came by way of Khanda to Khardaha.

910He bowed at the feet of Vasudha and Jahnava,
and both, laying a hand on him, blessed him.

911Prabhu Virachandra described to everyone
what had happened in Vrindavana.

912Here I have set it out only in brief —
I have recorded it in detail in the Virachandra-charita.

913Something of how Sri Virachandra Prabhu lived in renunciation
I have written in Prabhu's life.

914All the events that I write of in this book —
[I write] in constant remembrance of Prabhu's feet.

915All the shastras say that the guru's command is strongest:
whatever I have written, I wrote at the guru's command.

916He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the nineteenth vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.
